title: Sample 17-11: Omitted Letters Identified in Directions

illustrates.quote: a. Follow print for symbols used to show omission. A substitution may be made if accurate representation of the print symbol in braille would hinder the reader's recognition of the concept under discussion. Explain the choice of the substituted symbol in a transcriber's note.

blocks.text: Write each word, adding ie or ei. If you are not sure about a spelling, check the dictionary.

print.notes: A cell-5 heading, activity directions, an embedded transcriber's note explaining the print-square-to-braille-underscore substitution (17.9.2a's own 'explain the substitution' clause), then a 4-item numbered list of words with a single omitted-letter blank each.
print.printFeatures: Italic heading and directions; a light shaded square marks each omission in print.
print.transcriberNote: Print uses a square to represent the omission of letters, in braille an underscore is used for the omissions.
transcriberSupplied: the transcriber's note explaining the print square and the braille underscore (17.9.2a), and the substitution of an underscore for each printed square

braille.notes: Byte-identical between A and B; matches independent re-extraction exactly.

resolution: Both runs (A, B) came from the same model (Gemini Pro via Antigravity, 17 Sep 2026) and are not independent; agreement was treated as no evidence. braille.lines independently re-extracted from references/_text/braille-formats-2016.txt (the line-number field, digits + >=3 spaces, or the fixed left margin measured in ASCII spaces before any U+2800 cell, stripped by counting; U+2800->space; trailing spaces removed). Braille and rule id unchanged (normalised 'a.'/'a' spelling; both runs agreed on content, matches source). Modeled with a standalone 'note' block for the substitution explanation (block-level TN, 'done') and a lettered list whose items each carry one literal underscore standing for the blank-fill symbol. Print description corrected 23 Sep 2026 (see printCorrections).

printCorrections.evidence: references/_gemini/_done/gold-17-A/page-488.png: the print list reads "1. w[]ght  2. s[]ge  3. br[]f  4. v[]l" (numerals). Braille lines 8-11 begin #A4 #B4 #C4 #D4.

printCorrections.now: ...omission of letters, in braille an underscore...
printCorrections.evidence: references/_text/braille-formats-2016.txt line 14105 (braille line 6): "lrs1 9 brl an" - the punctuation cell after "letters" is 1 (comma), not 2 (semicolon); the note has a comma. (The note is the transcriber-supplied text in the braille, not print.)

printCorrections.was: a 'note' block "Print uses a square to represent the omission of letters, in braille an underscore is used for the omissions." before the list; item texts with underscores (w_ght, s_ge, br_f, v_l)
printCorrections.now: no note block (the note is in print.transcriberNote); item texts keep the printed square: w□ght, s□ge, br□f, v□l
printCorrections.evidence: references/bana/braille-formats-2016.pdf p.488, rendered at 110 dpi: the print original shows the heading, the directions and the numbered list 1. w□ght 2. s□ge 3. br□f 4. v□l with a square glyph. The note and the underscores are braille-side (transcriber) content.
